Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. One establishment identified but one criterion of the denominator called into question, hence the move to disputed. The University of Theatre and Film Arts in Budapest carries a puppet actor specialism whose first intake dates from 1995, in an integrated course, together with a puppet director specialism opened in 2008-09 within the directing course. Puppetry is therefore a named specialism of a higher education award, and the teaching criterion is satisfied. The institutional criterion no longer follows automatically: since 1 September 2020 the university is no longer a public institution but is run by a private foundation, a transfer that prompted a prolonged dispute over academic autonomy. The denominator requires a training backed by a state institution. Should that criterion be read as public ownership of the institution, in which case Hungary falls to 0, or as state recognition of the award plus public funding, in which case it counts 1? The value 1 is kept by default, the university remaining the national theatre and film school awarding recognised qualifications, but the status moves to disputed: what is in question is the counting method, not the existence of the training. A ruling is needed for the whole series, since the Hungarian model of transferring institutions to foundations affects the country's entire higher education system. Source caveat: the university's own site systematically refuses automated reading; the source recorded is an encyclopaedic entry, not the institution itself.

establishments.name: Színház- és Filmművészeti Egyetem (SZFE)
establishments.award: Puppet actor specialism since 1995, puppet director specialism since 2008-09
establishments.description: Hungary's national theatre and film university, teaching puppetry for thirty years. Transferred from state ownership to a private foundation in September 2020, which is why its place in this count is disputed rather than settled.

observations.reasoning: DISPUTED. First value produced as a mean conditioned on artists who actually tour, which drops from the denominator the makers who do not perform. Method error identified: a fee is not a performance. For France the true median probably sits between 10 and 20, over a bimodal distribution. For countries with permanent companies, recomputed from the top: 250 to 400 performances a year, casts of 3 to 5, a company of about twenty, so on the order of 50 to 90.
